title: A verified checkpoint of the real account is one 56.7 MB string: 8-13 s at 4x CPU and ~485 MB of extra heap, and the first cloud link, every import, reset and repair waits on it
detail: Copy account (the user's 26 Nov backup): KOS.backup.checkpoint('…') at 4x CPU took 12.7 s at mac and 8.0 s at iphone, ok:true, bytes 56.7 MB, and the page's used JS heap rose by 487 MB and 482 MB while it ran (performance.memory before/after, two runs). The snapshot is 30.8 MB of handwriting (140 ink pages, 34,318 strokes, 1.78 M points already packed as integers, so it is volume, not waste), 3.4 MB of Collection rows, 0.7 MB of state and the files' base64. One checkpoint holds the snapshot object, its JSON text, the text read back from IndexedDB, its parse and a second live snapshot at once (backup.js:168-196), which is where the heap goes. Five are kept: about 280 MB of IndexedDB on this account. The streamed backup FILE of the same data (KOS.backupFile.write, DI-09) builds in about 1 s with nothing missing. CLAUDE.md names the one-string checkpoint as a known limit for a very large file set; this account is already there because of ink alone, and it grows with every page written. On an iPhone or iPad tab a ~0.5 GB spike risks the WebContent process being killed in the middle of 'Before linking this device to the cloud' (cloudsync.js:879-881), which the first link requires (invariant 34), or before an import/reset (dataview.js:106, 345).
rootCause: js/core/backup.js:168-196 attempt() — JSON.stringify of the whole snapshotFull (backup.js:136-141, store.js:1335) into one string, stored as one record, read back whole and parsed whole, then snapshotFull again for the live check; nothing is split per part or streamed as KOS.backupFile already does.
evidence: eval at 4x CPU: mac {ok:true, mb:56.7, ms:12704, heapMB:487}, iphone {ok:true, mb:56.7, ms:7992, heapMB:482}; snapshotFull parts: ink 32.3 M chars, mediaEntries 3.4 M, state 0.68 M; ink pages 140, median 126 KB, largest 819 KB; /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/copy/cdp.mjs
fix: Store a checkpoint as one record per part (and per file / per ink doc), each with its own SHA-256, and verify part by part — reuse KOS.backupFile's per-line layout — so no step holds the whole account as one string; keep fewer checkpoints when they are large.
